snippets.text: Parsimony, an open-source benchmark posted to Show HN, ranks coding models by how much net code they add to solved SWE-bench tasks, counting statements and calls rather than lines.
snippets.why: Existing coding benchmarks reward solve rate and cost, so a measure of bloat adds a missing axis for anyone choosing a model to maintain code.

snippets.text: X user thsottiaux, who posts a daily series of ChatGPT and Codex updates, says a desktop app change cuts the state stored on disk by 60%, after power users ran out of space.
snippets.why: Heavy Codex users had been filling their drives with local agent history, so the fix lands on the people running long sessions.

snippets.text: ComfyUI says NVIDIA's RTX VFX nodes are now in the app, with EXR file support, RTX Video Super Resolution, Frame Generation and SDR-to-HDR conversion, all running locally on RTX GPUs.
snippets.why: Chaining the three nodes lets VFX artists finish AI footage on their own hardware before it returns to a compositing pipeline.

snippets.text: Developer Theo says ts-rust v0.6.0 is 30% faster than the last release and up to 70% faster in a new --fast mode that trades memory for speed, while staying compatible with upstream TypeScript.
snippets.why: The project aims to close the speed gap with Bun's type checker while keeping full TypeScript compatibility, which Theo says Bun does not.

snippets.text: Artificial Analysis says Anthropic's Sonnet 5.5 tops its Coding Agent Index at 68 in Claude Code at max effort; xhigh scores 63 at $3.33 a task against $14.19.
snippets.why: The gap shows what the last five index points cost: more than four times the spend per task for a modest gain.

snippets.text: Vals AI says it asked Chinese and American models hundreds of sensitive questions about China; it reports MiMo V2.6 Pro and GLM-5.3 sometimes criticise China, while Gemini 4 Argon, Mistral Large 4 and Grok 4.7 occasionally repeat CCP propaganda.
snippets.why: The result cuts against the assumption that Chinese-built models are the more deferential ones, though it is one benchmark firm's test.

snippets.text: Intelligence-focused X account IntCyberDigest says XBOW researchers earned a $250,000 Google reward for a Chrome exploit chaining three bugs, built in six days with OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol for about $40,000 of compute.
snippets.why: XBOW's own posts describe the award but name no model, and Google has not confirmed it, so the model detail is unverified.

snippets.text: Nanya Technology told investors on its earnings call that a prolonged AI-driven DRAM shortage is likely and hard to resolve through 2027 into early 2028, according to analyst jukan05.
snippets.why: A major memory maker expecting tight supply for years points to higher prices for the chips that go into AI servers and ordinary devices.

snippets.text: Bloomberg reports, per The Verge, that Epic Games has given developers on an unannounced Disney game an "AI-first" mandate, with tools like Anthropic's Claude used to finish code and art, and the game is delayed from March.
snippets.why: It is a large studio publicly steering a delayed flagship project toward generated code and art, which is likely to draw scrutiny from artists.

snippets.text: The Information reports that OpenAI is scrambling to fix safety issues involving loop transformers before shipping its next flagship model, according to a Techmeme summary; the outlet is the only one with the report so far.
snippets.why: If accurate, it suggests the next OpenAI flagship may use an unusual architecture that the company is still working to make safe.

snippets.text: The Information reports, per Techmeme, that OpenAI is in early talks to buy security startup Trail of Bits, which finds and fixes vulnerabilities in open-source software; no deal has been confirmed.
snippets.why: Trail of Bits already works with OpenAI on its Patch the Planet initiative, so a purchase would deepen an existing relationship.

snippets.text: Developer Sammy Straus says a Hacker News post sent his feed-reader site into days of slowdown, with nearly half of traffic from one AI-newsletter scraper, which he blocked; the post has 256 points.
snippets.why: It is a first-hand example of how AI crawlers and scrapers can overwhelm a small site after a front-page launch.
